issue.title: linux: duplicate tray icon on COSMIC — dropTrayName() re-registers an item the watcher kept
issue.body:
## What happens

On COSMIC (Wayland), the tray icon shows up twice in the panel — two identical
magpie icons for one running instance.

`RegisteredStatusNotifierItems` on the StatusNotifierWatcher has two entries for
the same process:

```
:1.1004/StatusNotifierItem
:1.1004
```

Both resolve to `/StatusNotifierItem`, both report `Id: magpie`, same
`Menu: /StatusNotifierMenu`. Nothing else is duplicated — magpie is the only
app with two entries.

The duplicate is not a one-off: it comes back on every start of magpie.

## Why

`internal/gui/bus_linux.go`, `dropTrayName()`:

1. Wails' tray takes `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` and registers with the
   watcher.
2. `dropTrayName()` releases that name and registers again with
   `conn.Names()[0]` (`:1.x`), on the assumption that a watcher which filed the
   item under the name it was given up by drops it with the name (the comment
   cites Quickshell/noctalia and #2421) — so the second registration restores
   the item rather than adding one.

COSMIC's watcher (`cosmic-applet-status-area --status-notifier-watcher`) files
the item under the **sender's own unique name** plus `/StatusNotifierItem`, not
under the well-known name it was registered with. Releasing
`org.kde.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` therefore does not remove that entry, and
the re-registration is a different string — so it is a second item, not a
replacement.

## Steps to reproduce

1. COSMIC Wayland session, `cosmic-applet-status-area` running (it owns
   `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` and `com.system76.CosmicStatusNotifierWatcher`).
2. Start magpie; let it create the tray item, wait for `dropTrayName()` to run.
3. `gdbus call --session --dest org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher \
     --object-path /StatusNotifierWatcher \
     --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get \
     org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher RegisteredStatusNotifierItems`
4. Two entries for magpie; two icons in the panel.

## Suggested fix

The precondition the workaround relies on is not universal: on any watcher that
keeps the item when the name is released, the second registration duplicates it.
The spec has no requirement for a watcher to merge `:1.x` and
`:1.x/StatusNotifierItem` — they are different keys — so the extra registration
is what creates the second icon.

Rather than special-casing COSMIC, ask the watcher whether the item survived:

```go
if _, err := conn.ReleaseName(name); err != nil { ... }
own := conn.Names()
if len(own) == 0 {
    return
}
w := conn.Object("org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher", "/StatusNotifierWatcher")
// A watcher that keeps the item when the name is released already has it
// filed under our unique name: registering again adds a second icon.
var items []string
if err := w.GetProperty("org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher.RegisteredStatusNotifierItems").Store(&items); err == nil {
    for _, it := range items {
        if it == own[0] || strings.HasPrefix(it, own[0]+"/") {
            return
        }
    }
}
if c := w.Call("org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher.RegisterStatusNotifierItem", 0, own[0]); c.Err != nil { ... }
```

That keeps the noctalia/Quickshell case working (item gone → register again) and
leaves COSMIC with the single item it already has.

## Environment

- magpie 0.1.1285 (v0.1.1285), built from source
- COSMIC 1.9.0: cosmic-applets 1.9.0 (`cosmic-applet-status-area`, owns
  `com.system76.CosmicStatusNotifierWatcher`), cosmic-panel 1.9.0
- NixOS, Wayland session

comments.body:
The duplicate is `dropTrayName` registering the item a second time regardless of what the watcher did with the released name.

`dropTrayName` (`internal/gui/bus_linux.go`) releases `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` and then always calls `RegisterStatusNotifierItem` with the connection's own name, on the premise that the watcher dropped the item together with the released name. COSMIC files the item under the sender's own name and keeps it, so that call adds a second item instead of restoring the first one: the `:1.x/StatusNotifierItem` and `:1.x` pair in the report.

The branch asks the watcher first. After the release it reads `RegisteredStatusNotifierItems` from `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` and, when the item is already listed under the connection's own name (that name, or a path under it), it does not register again. A watcher that dropped the item with the name still gets the registration, so the noctalia/Quickshell case from #2421 is unchanged, and a property read that fails keeps the old behavior.

[fix/2804-linux-duplicate-tray-icon-on](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/2804-linux-duplicate-tray-icon-on), commit 7256f0d91a64c285831e38172d81906a31d890a9

Ran: `TestTrayReleasedNameKeepsOneItem` (internal/gui) starts a `dbus-daemon` of its own, owns `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` on it, and models both watcher shapes. Without the change the COSMIC case failed with `the panel lists 2 magpie items [":1.1/StatusNotifierItem" ":1.1"] after the name was released, want 1`; with it both cases pass, as does `-race -count=5` (15 passed). `go test ./internal/gui/ -count=1` ok (43.077s); `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/gui/` and `gofmt -l` clean; the test also passes in a `-tags nogui` build. Not tried: COSMIC itself, since a GOOS build is not a test, so a check of the panel with this branch would be welcome.

This is a fork branch, ready for review; it makes no claim on the issue's ownership.

I tested `7256f0d9` on a real NixOS + COSMIC Wayland session. I built Magpie 0.1.1866 from a Nix package with this patch applied and the narrower `CosmicStatusNotifierWatcher` workaround removed; the validation branch is https://github.com/mtul0729/nixpkgs/tree/test/magpie-3372-2804 .

I launched the patched `magpie tray` with an isolated temporary `HOME`/XDG config on the live session bus, so the panel used the real `com.system76.CosmicStatusNotifierWatcher`. After `dropTrayName` had run:

- `GetNameOwner org.kde.StatusNotifierItem-17071-1` returned `The name does not have an owner`.
- `RegisteredStatusNotifierItems` contained exactly one item for that process's connection: `:1.4881/StatusNotifierItem`.
- `GetConnectionUnixProcessID(:1.4881)` returned the test PID, 17071.
- There was no second `:1.4881` entry.

Stopping the test instance removed its item; the separately running Magpie instance was untouched. This is the list COSMIC's panel consumes, and the real watcher now shows one magpie item for the patched process.
